humanReviewCriteria: Ava sounds warm and engaging without imitating a child or becoming cartoonish.
The same recognizable voice identity is preserved across every delivery.
Pacing is clear enough for a child and does not sound slow, robotic or singsong.
Emphasis and pauses create usable co-speech motion beats without overacting.
Generated body motion has a clear semantic purpose and is not symmetric arm flapping.
The torso, gaze, head and hands support one another while feet remain planted.
Motion begins from and returns to Ava's relaxed living idle without a snap.
Repeated semantic intentions still produce plausible variation rather than duplication.

cases.text: Hi! I'm Ava. It's really nice to see you.
motionReviewFocus: Small welcoming acknowledgement rather than a large wave.
Soft forward attention followed by a clean return to neutral.

cases.text: That sounds fun. What was the best part?
motionReviewFocus: Curious head and gaze behavior supports the question.
No unnecessary two-handed explanatory gesture.

cases.text: Hmm, let me think. I believe the smaller one will fit.
motionReviewFocus: Reflection and answer are visibly different phases.
Thinking-away gaze resolves back to eye contact.

cases.text: Plants lean toward light because their growing cells respond to where the light is coming from.
motionReviewFocus: One asymmetric explanatory gesture follows sentence emphasis.
Torso support is subtle and the arms never float without purpose.

cases.text: Let's count them together: one, two, three, and four.
motionReviewFocus: Counting beats align clearly with the four spoken numbers.
Finger or hand accents stay readable without becoming rigid.

cases.text: This shape is taller, but this one is wider. They are different in two useful ways.
motionReviewFocus: Left and right ideas are distinct without mirrored arm flapping.
Gaze and torso handoffs make the comparison easy to follow.

cases.text: Look at the picture below. The highlighted piece is one part out of four equal parts.
motionReviewFocus: Ava presents the lower dashboard rather than pointing at empty space.
She returns eye contact after introducing the visual.

cases.text: You were very close. Try that last step once more; I know you can do it.
motionReviewFocus: Supportive openness stays restrained and sincere.
No cheering pose or repetitive upward hand pumping.

cases.text: It's okay to feel stuck. We can slow down and work through it together.
motionReviewFocus: Concern reads as attentive calm rather than sadness or alarm.
Body motion remains open, safe and non-intrusive.

cases.text: Yes, that's it! You found the pattern.
motionReviewFocus: Celebration is bright but small enough to transition naturally.
Hands, face and upper body peak together without foot sliding.
